A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new theory to understand the structure of preferential attachment graphs, and have used it to develop efficient compression algorithms that are provably optimal.
we have developed a novel framework for compression of structural information in graphs that is both efficient (in the algorithmic sense) and optimal (in the information-theoretic sense).

we give the first algorithms that asymptotically approach the Shannon entropy for both unlabeled and labelled scale free graphs, and that we give new results that allow us to characterize the number of symmetrical structures for the preferential attachment graph model for all parameters of the model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Shannon entropy of a graph can be estimated by analyzing the structure of the graph itself.

, for preferential attachment graphs, the asymptotic compression ratio is essentially independent of the label alphabet size and is equal to (log m)/(log log n) for the unlabeled case, and (log m)/(m log log n) for labeled graphs.

, in spite of the fact that the model is not memoryless (and hence the Shannon entropy does not give a lower bound on the compression length), we can still use it to give asymptotically optimal compression schemes, and, furthermore, we can do it algorithmically.
